title: Ensure MFA is enabled for the root account
description: The root account has unrestricted access to all resources. Without MFA, a compromised password gives an attacker full control of the entire AWS environment.

remediation.description: Enable MFA on the root account via the IAM console.

title: Ensure IAM password policy requires minimum length >= 14
description: Short passwords are vulnerable to brute-force attacks. A minimum length of 14 characters significantly increases resistance to password guessing.

remediation.description: Set the minimum password length to 14 or higher.

title: Ensure IAM password policy prevents password reuse
description: Without password reuse prevention, users can cycle back to previously compromised passwords.

remediation.description: Set password reuse prevention to remember at least 24 previous passwords.

title: Ensure IAM users have MFA enabled
description: Without MFA, IAM user accounts are vulnerable to credential theft. MFA adds a second layer of authentication beyond passwords.

remediation.description: Enable MFA for all IAM users with console access.

title: Ensure no access keys exist for the root account
description: Root access keys provide unrestricted access and cannot be limited by IAM policies. If leaked, an attacker has full control with no audit trail attribution.

remediation.description: Delete all root account access keys.

title: Ensure access keys are rotated within 90 days
description: Long-lived access keys increase the window of exposure if a key is compromised. Regular rotation limits the blast radius of credential leaks.

remediation.description: Rotate access keys that are older than 90 days.
remediation.command: aws iam create-access-key --user-name <USER> && aws iam delete-access-key --user-name <USER> --access-key-id <OLD_KEY>

title: Ensure CloudTrail is enabled in all regions
description: Without multi-region CloudTrail, API activity in non-primary regions goes unlogged. Attackers can operate in unmonitored regions to avoid detection.

title: Ensure CloudTrail log file validation is enabled
description: Without log file validation, an attacker could tamper with or delete CloudTrail logs without detection.

remediation.description: Enable log file validation on all trails.

title: Ensure CloudTrail logs are encrypted with KMS
description: Unencrypted CloudTrail logs stored in S3 could be read by anyone with bucket access. KMS encryption adds a layer of access control.

remediation.description: Enable KMS encryption on CloudTrail trails.

title: Ensure VPC flow logs are enabled
description: Without VPC flow logs, network traffic is invisible. You cannot detect unusual traffic patterns, data exfiltration, or lateral movement within your VPC.

remediation.description: Enable VPC flow logs for all VPCs.
remediation.command: aws ec2 create-flow-logs --resource-type VPC --resource-ids <VPC_ID> --traffic-type ALL --log-destination-type cloud-watch-logs --log-group-name vpc-flow-logs

title: Ensure no security groups allow ingress 0.0.0.0/0 to port 22
description: SSH open to the world is the most common attack vector for cloud instances. Automated scanners continuously probe port 22 across all public IPs.

remediation.description: Restrict SSH access to specific IP ranges.

title: Ensure no security groups allow ingress 0.0.0.0/0 to port 3389
description: RDP open to the world exposes Windows instances to brute-force attacks. RDP vulnerabilities like BlueKeep can be exploited remotely.

remediation.description: Restrict RDP access to specific IP ranges.

title: Ensure the default security group restricts all traffic
description: The default security group allows all outbound traffic and all inbound traffic from the same group. If resources are accidentally placed in it, they may be more exposed than intended.

remediation.description: Remove all inbound and outbound rules from the default security group.
consoleSteps: Remove all inbound and outbound rules

title: Ensure S3 bucket public access is blocked at account level
description: Without account-level S3 public access blocking, any bucket can be made public — accidentally or by a compromised IAM user. This is the #1 cause of S3 data breaches.

remediation.description: Enable S3 Block Public Access at the account level.

title: Ensure S3 buckets have server-side encryption enabled
description: Unencrypted S3 objects are readable by anyone with access to the underlying storage. Encryption at rest protects data if physical media is compromised.

remediation.description: Enable default encryption on all S3 buckets.

title: Ensure S3 bucket versioning is enabled
description: Without versioning, deleted or overwritten objects are permanently lost. Versioning provides a safety net against accidental deletion and ransomware attacks.

remediation.description: Enable versioning on all S3 buckets.
